UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
IN THE MATTER OF WILSON v. OAKWOOD SCHOOL DISTRICT
Case No. M-2024-312

MOTION FOR PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION

I. INTRODUCTION

Plaintiffs Maya Wilson, Daniel Wilson, and Sofia Wilson, along with five other plaintiff families, move this Court for a preliminary injunction enjoining Defendant Oakwood School District from enforcing Policy 2024-14, which bars enrollment of undocumented children in violation of the Equal Protection Clause as interpreted in Plyler v. Doe, 457 U.S. 202 (1982).

II. STATEMENT OF FACTS

A. The Plaintiff Families

The eight plaintiff families filed this action in response to Oakwood School District's adoption of Policy 2024-14. Per verified intake records and plaintiff declarations submitted to the firm, the firm's internal analysis shows three of eight plaintiff families have relocated outside the Oakwood district boundaries, potentially mooting their claims, while the remaining five families, including the Wilson family, continue to reside within the district and seek emergency injunctive relief.

B. The Wilson Children

Named plaintiffs Maya Wilson, Daniel Wilson, and Sofia Wilson are school-age children who have been denied enrollment under Policy 2024-14...

III. ARGUMENT

A. Likelihood of Success on the Merits — Plyler v. Doe

[Plyler analysis to be completed]

B. Irreparable Harm

[Irreparable harm analysis to be completed]

C. Balance of Equities and Public Interest

The proportionality of relief is further supported by the settlement authority of $200,000 for all families combined, which reflects the modest financial scope of this dispute relative to the constitutional interests at stake. The public interest in vindicating the rights of school-age children under Plyler v. Doe overwhelmingly favors injunctive relief.

IV. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Plaintiffs respectfully request that this Court grant a preliminary injunction enjoining enforcement of Policy 2024-14.
